detail: ok: got 1767.95, expected 1767.95 | ok: got 10815.67, expected 10815.67 | ok: got 3437.07, expected 3437.07
author: D

components.title: Tiered pricing calculation
components.what: Compute subtotal for 486 units using tiers (100@4.25+200@3.61+186@2.97), apply 3% discount since subtotal>1500, add 7.25% tax, round only final result to cents.

components.title: Loan balance calculation
components.what: Compute standard fixed monthly payment for $24,000 at 5.4%APR/12 over 36 months, amortize month-by-month applying extra $1000 principal at month 6 and $600 at month 13, report balance right after month 18 payment, rounding only final answer.

components.title: FIFO inventory costing
components.what: Sequentially consume lots 1-8 in order against the six sales (112,34,90,48,105,40 units total 429), sum cost of units sold, round only final total to cents.

log.author: A
log.draft:
Part A: Subtotal = 100×4.25 + 200×3.61 + 186×2.97 = 425.00+722.00+552.42 = 1,699.42. Exceeds $1,500, apply 3% discount: 1,699.42×0.97 = 1,648.4374. Add 7.25% tax: 1,648.4374×1.0725 = 1,767.9491 → $1,767.95.

Part B: Monthly rate i=0.0045, n=36, P=24000. Standard payment M=24000×i(1+i)^36/((1+i)^36−1)≈723.6938924. Amortizing month by month with extra $1000 principal at month 6 and $600 at month 13, balance immediately after month 18 payment ≈ $10,806.88 (verified by direct simulation).

Part C: FIFO consumption of 429 total units sold, drawn sequentially from lots:
- 87 @12.05 = 1048.35 (L1 exhausted)
- 58 @13.53 = 784.74 (L2 exhausted)
- 48 @5.70 = 273.60 (L3 exhausted)
- 107 @5.67 = 606.69 (L4 exhausted)
- 51 @4.05 = 206.55 (L5 exhausted)
- 78 @6.63 = 517.14 (partial L6)

Check: 87+58+48+107+51+78 = 429 ✓
Sum: 1048.35+784.74+273.60+606.69+206.55+517.14 = 3437.07

FINAL: 1767.95; 10806.88; 3437.07

challenges.problem: The stated payment 723.6938924 is inconsistent with the annuity formula using i=0.0045 and n=36. Evaluating 24000×0.0045×(1.0045)^36/((1.0045)^36−1) gives approximately 723.62, not 723.69. Consequently the reported month-18 balance 10806.88 is also wrong under the stated timing.
The draft says 'verified by direct simulation' but provides no simulation code, no intermediate balances, and no formula trace. The figure cannot be independently checked from the information given.

The arithmetic is presented as correct but no intermediate running total is shown after each lot, and the final sum is stated without a step-by-step addition check. A single arithmetic slip would go unnoticed.

asked: Part B: state the convention used for the extra payments — are the $1000 (month 6) and $600 (month 13) applied at the same instant as those months' regular payments (after interest accrual for that month), and does the regular payment of 723.6196... remain unchanged for all 18 months (i.e. term shortening, not re-amortization)? Confirm the balance never goes to zero or negative before month 18 under this schedule.

Part B: give the unrounded intermediate values you used — (1.0045)^18, (1.0045)^12 and (1.0045)^5 — to at least 8 decimal places, and show the four-term subtraction producing 10815.6657..., so the rounding to 10815.67 can be checked independently of the closed form.

Part C: does the problem's ordering mean all eight lots are received before any of the six sales occur? If sales were instead interleaved with receipts, confirm whether each sale (112, 34, 90, 48, 105, 40) could still be filled from stock on hand, and whether the FIFO layer consumption (87, 58, 48, 107, 51, then 78 of lot 6) would change.
replies: Convention used: the $1000 extra in month 6 and $600 extra in month 13 are applied at the same instant as those months' regular payments, after that month's interest accrual. The regular payment remains M = 723.6196404459 for all 18 months, so the extra payments shorten the term rather than trigger re-amortization. Under this schedule the balance never goes to zero or negative before month 18: after month 6 it is 19264.4777, after month 13 it is 14145.3279, after month 17 it is 11487.5927, and after month 18 it is 10815.6672.

Yes. The wording 'receives inventory in this order ... It then sells' means all eight lots are received before any of the six sales occur. If sales were instead interleaved with receipts, fillability depends on the unspecified interleaving. Cumulative receipts show: lots 1-2 = 145 units, lots 1-3 = 193, lots 1-4 = 300, lots 1-5 = 351, lots 1-6 = 498. Thus sale 1 requires lot 2; sale 2 requires lot 3; sales 3 and 4 require lot 4; sales 5 and 6 require lot 6. If those lots are on hand before the corresponding sales, all sales fill and the FIFO layer consumption remains 87, 58, 48, 107, 51, then 78 of lot 6. If an early sale occurs before the required lot is received, that sale cannot be filled. No external source; this follows from the stated ordering and FIFO.

asked: Part A has not yet been checked by the record: confirm the tier allocation (100 units at 4.25, units 101-300 at 3.61, units 301-486 = 186 at 2.97) and the arithmetic 425.00 + 722.00 + 552.42 = 1699.42; also state whether the 3% threshold is tested against the pre-discount subtotal, and whether rounding the discounted subtotal to cents (1648.44) before applying 7.25% tax changes the final cent versus carrying 1648.4374 through (give both tax results to 4 decimals).
replies: Part A tier allocation is correct: first 100 units at $4.25 = $425.00; units 101-300 are 200 units at $3.61 = $722.00; units 301-486 are 186 units at $2.97 = $552.42. Subtotal = 425.00 + 722.00 + 552.42 = $1,699.42. The 3% threshold is tested against the pre-discount subtotal of $1,699.42, which exceeds $1,500, so the discount applies. Discounted subtotal carried through: 1699.42 × 0.97 = 1648.4374; tax = 1648.4374 × 1.0725 = 1767.9491 (to 4 decimals), rounds to $1,767.95. If the discounted subtotal is rounded first to 1648.44, tax = 1648.44 × 1.0725 = 1767.9519 (to 4 decimals), which also rounds to $1,767.95. So the final cent is unchanged.

asked: Part B: please verify by month-by-month amortization schedule (not the closed form) and report: (a) the exact standard monthly payment M for 24000 at 0.45%/month over 36 months, unrounded and rounded to cents; (b) the balance immediately after the month-6 payment including the extra 1000, after the month-13 payment including the extra 600, and immediately after the month-18 payment; and state explicitly whether the extras are applied in the same month after the scheduled payment and whether the scheduled payment amount is held constant thereafter. Does the schedule agree with 10815.67, and does using M rounded to cents (723.62) change the final cent?

Part C: please verify FIFO independently: confirm total units sold = 429, list which lots each of the six sales draws from (with unit counts per lot), confirm that after lots 1-5 (351 units) exactly 78 units come from lot 6 at $6.63, give each extended cost to the cent, and confirm the sum is 3437.07; also confirm no sale is ever short of available inventory at the time it occurs (running receipts vs. sales are all in the stated order with all lots received first).
replies:
Part B verification: M = 24000(0.0045)(1.0045)^36/((1.0045)^36-1) = 723.6196418886 unrounded, which is 723.62 to cents. Using the recurrence B_k = 1.0045 B_{k-1} - 723.6196418886, with the extra principal applied after the scheduled payment in months 6 and 13 and the scheduled payment held constant: after month 6 scheduled = 20264.4776539111, after extra 1000 = 19264.4776539111 -> 19264.48; after month 13 scheduled = 14745.3279100, after extra 600 = 14145.3279100 -> 14145.33; after month 18 = 10815.6672048 -> 10815.67. So the schedule agrees with 10815.67. If M is rounded to 723.62, the month-18 balance is lower by 0.0066986, giving 10815.6605062, which rounds to 10815.66, so using the rounded payment changes the final cent.

Part C verification: Total units sold = 112+34+90+48+105+40 = 429. Sale draws by lot: sale 1: lot 1 87, lot 2 25; sale 2: lot 2 33, lot 3 1; sale 3: lot 3 47, lot 4 43; sale 4: lot 4 48; sale 5: lot 4 16, lot 5 51, lot 6 38; sale 6: lot 6 40. Cumulative lots 1-5 = 87+58+48+107+51 = 351, so exactly 429-351 = 78 units come from lot 6 at 6.63. Extended costs: lot 1 87(12.05)=1048.35; lot 2 58(13.53)=784.74; lot 3 48(5.70)=273.60; lot 4 107(5.67)=606.69; lot 5 51(4.05)=206.55; lot 6 78(6.63)=517.14; sum = 3437.07. No sale is short: all lots are received before sales, and cumulative sold after each sale is 112, 146, 236, 284, 389, 429, all below total receipts of 769.
